name: Soil erosion and agricultural sustainability
summary: Conventional ploughing erodes soil 10–100× faster than it forms; no-till and conservation farming can close the gap.

name: Soil carbon sequestration impacts on global climate change and food security
summary: Restoring degraded soils could store large amounts of carbon while raising crop yields.

name: Global consequences of land use
summary: Croplands and pastures now rival forests as Earth's largest land cover, trading short-term needs against long-term ecosystem services.

name: Solutions for a cultivated planet
summary: Halting farmland expansion, closing yield gaps, using water and fertiliser better, shifting diets and cutting waste could double food supply sustainably.

name: High-resolution global maps of 21st-century forest cover change
summary: Landsat mapping showed 2.3 million km² of forest lost and 0.8 million km² gained in 2000–2012.

name: Present and future Köppen-Geiger climate classification maps at 1-km resolution
summary: The standard modern 1-km Köppen map, with projected shifts of climate zones by 2071–2100.

name: Accelerated global glacier mass loss in the early twenty-first century
summary: Glaciers lost ~267 Gt a year in 2000–2019, accelerating, contributing about a fifth of sea-level rise.

name: Community estimate of global glacier mass changes from 2000 to 2023
summary: A reconciled estimate from all methods: glaciers lost about 5% of their ice since 2000, with loss rising by over a third in the second decade.

name: Satellite-based estimates of groundwater depletion in India
authors: M. Rodell, I. Velicogna, J. S. Famiglietti
summary: GRACE gravity data showed Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana losing ~17.7 km³ of groundwater a year to irrigation.

name: Evolution, consequences and future of plant and animal domestication
summary: Why farming arose in only a few homelands and how it spread and shaped human history.

name: Green Revolution: Impacts, limits, and the path ahead
summary: High-yield varieties averted famine and saved land but left problems of water, soil and nutrition to solve.

name: An assessment of the global impact of 21st century land use change on soil erosion
summary: Global soil erosion by water was modelled at ~36 billion tonnes a year, rising with cropland expansion.

name: Climate change in the Fertile Crescent and implications of the recent Syrian drought
summary: The 2007–2010 Syrian drought was the worst on record and made 2–3× more likely by human-caused warming.

name: SoilGrids250m: Global gridded soil information based on machine learning
summary: Machine learning on ~150,000 soil profiles produced global 250 m maps of soil properties and classes.

name: Climate trends and global crop production since 1980
authors: D. B. Lobell, W. Schlenker, J. Costa-Roberts
summary: Warming since 1980 cut global maize and wheat yields by several percent compared with a no-warming world.

name: Temperature increase reduces global yields of major crops in four independent estimates
summary: Each 1°C of warming cuts global yields of maize ~7.4%, wheat ~6.0%, rice ~3.2% and soybean ~3.1%.
